svg.title: Kitchen lighting: 12 V RGB best-practice breadboard proof of concept
svg.desc: Nano 33 IoT, two TC4427ACPA drivers, three IRFZ44NPBF MOSFETs and a breadboard barrel jack. Paired wire labels identify both ends of one jumper. Output a40 +12 V, a41 green, a42 red, a43 blue. Only a short 12 V strip segment is connected.
svg.text: Kitchen lighting · 12 V RGB · best practice
All components on the board · Nano 33 IoT USB at top · side rails unused
Start with ONE marked cut segment. Maximum test length: 25 cm (0.30 A LED load at 14.4 W/m).
Use the existing 12 V supply. Its 6 A rating is capacity, not a breadboard fault-current limit. The full spool stays disconnected.
Read this as a physical top view
A label at two holes means ONE insulated jumper between those holes.
For example, P1 is i10 ↔ a22. The jumper table below lists both ends of each wire.
a–e connect across each row; f–j connect across each row. The trench isolates them.
Nano: c1–c15 / g1–g15. U1 and U2 notches point UP toward the USB socket.
Pins 1/8 are NC. U2 pin 4 is grounded; U2 pin 5 is left unconnected.
R1–R3 and R7–R9 = 10 kΩ. R4–R6 = 100 Ω. All are ¼ W.
Use upright axial resistors; bend each return lead down to its listed second hole.
Q3: G g47, D g48, S g49. Printed fronts face LEFT; packages stand upright.
J0: center pin 1 b58; sleeve pin 2 b60; switched pin 3 d59 is UNUSED.
Jack opening faces DOWN. Gently form its non-grid leads; do not force the body.
Power jumpers leave at e58/e60, clear of J0. Leave row 59 left bank isolated.
C7 is optional: 100 µF / 25 V; + h60, − h62. Form its leads as needed.
Jumper list · plug one end into each listed hole
Orientation check before inserting the MOSFETs
Front view: G · D · S, left to right. Metal tab = drain.
On this board, turn the printed front toward the a / left edge.
Then the gate goes in the smallest row number, source in the largest.
The narrow rectangles on the board are the upright packages seen edge-on.
Their three leads MUST occupy three separate rows, never one row.
TO-220 leads may be too thick for some breadboards. Insert only if they seat normally;
do not force them. Use suitable thin-pin adapters if needed; package sizes are illustrative.
The jack also needs small lead bends: its actual pin spacing is 3 / 6 mm, not 2.54 / 5.08 mm.
Power OFF before rewiring. Check for shorts, electrolytic polarity, and center-positive 12 V at the jack before connecting the board.
Start with one cut segment; measure actual current before extending to ≤25 cm. The 0.30 A figure covers LEDs, plus Nano/driver current.
USB-only programming with 12 V off: unplug P1 / P2 / P3 at i10 / i8 / i7. Keep all three MOSFET tabs from touching other leads.
5 V strip, buck converter and level shifter are not installed. L7805CV regulators and the original controller are not used.
REV H · 12 OCT 2026 · Short-strip proof of concept. Final full-strip wiring needs a current-rated PCB or soldered assembly.
